Calm Breath

Practice sitting or lying down, never while driving. If you feel out of breath, stop and return to your natural breath. It usually means you’re not breathing properly yet, and that’s something we teach. Download our free app and start with deep belly breathing, or reach out.

Shallow breathing fuels the mental health crisis.

If you live with anxiety, panic, burnout or depression, there’s a good chance you breathe short and shallow without realizing it. Over time, that pattern can become over-breathing: you take in more air than your body needs, your carbon dioxide drops, and your nervous system stays on alert. You end up feeling lightheaded, tense, wired and tired all at once. The good news: breathing is a skill, and skills can be trained. BEAT + BREATH™, our signature method, teaches you to take command of your breath and slow it down to 4 to 10 breaths a minute. Yes, it’s possible, and the research agrees.

A 2018 review of the research linked slow breathing, under 10 breaths a minute, with more relaxation and alertness and with fewer symptoms of anxiety. Read the review in Frontiers in Human Neuroscience. In a 2023 Stanford study, five minutes of breathwork a day for a month, especially breathing with a long exhale, improved mood and lowered breathing rate more than the same time spent in mindfulness meditation. Read the study in Cell Reports Medicine.

Don’t take our word for it. Take 60 seconds to count your breaths.

How many breaths do you take in a minute? Take a guess, then press start and find out.

most breathing apps hand you a timer and silence to sit through.

We hand you a beat.

BEAT + BREATH™ is our signature method. It slows your breath down with a steady beat and a count out loud.

  • The beat

    Your body loves rhythm. Follow a steady and slow beat and feel your nervous system regulate itself.

  • The breath

    The beat trains you to breathe on command, making it easier to slow your breath down when you need to.

  • The count

    We count out loud to engage your mind and keep it focused and sharp on the task at hand.

BEAT + BREATH™: five breaths, three lengths, forty-five tracks.

An audio-based breath training. Each breath is a different pattern of breathing in, pausing and breathing out, set to its own track and counted out loud, so you can train your breath one count at a time. Each level has fifteen tracks: the five breaths at three counts (4, 5 and 6 seconds at Level 1). Paces shown at Level 1.

The five BEAT + BREATH breaths
CoverBreathPatternMade forBreaths a minute
Basic Inhale 4, exhale 4 Training your everyday breath to be slower and steadier 7½
Bridge Inhale 4, pause 4, exhale 4 Settling emotions and building lung capacity 5
Box Inhale 4, pause 4, exhale 4, pause 4 Grounding yourself under pressure 3¾
Calm Inhale 4, exhale 6 Easing tension before bed or after a stressful stretch 6
Super Calm Inhale 4, exhale 4, pause 8 The “about to scream or cry” moments 3¾
  1. 3 minLevel 1, Monkey MindBreaths of 4 to 6 seconds. For new breathers, or anyone too frazzled for more.
  2. 5 minLevel 2, ApprenticeBreaths of 7 to 9 seconds. Move up when Level 1 feels easy.
  3. 11 minLevel 3, Almost EnlightenedBreaths of 10 to 12 seconds. For when you’re ready to go deeper.

A psychotherapist and a composer made a record you breathe to.

Esther Kalaba, MA, RP, is a Registered Psychotherapist licensed in Ontario and Quebec. She has been a therapist for 20 years and a daily meditator for over 20 years. She has taught breathing to kids as young as five and adults well into their eighties: about 500 people through Begin with Breath alone, and roughly 1,200 live mornings of practice since 2021.

Ma’amo Koba is a Grammy nominated composer and producer, with credits at NASA, HBO and Apple. He wrote the rhythm and the music every track runs on.

“Our mission is to integrate simple and effective breathing practices into the fabric of daily life, so that conscious breathing is your first response to any stressful situation.”

People of the Prana offers breath education. It is not psychotherapy and is not a replacement for medical or psychological advice, diagnosis or treatment. Please consult your health care provider before starting a new practice, especially if you have a medical or mental health condition.
